Rashi on Shabbat 32b:1:1.hebrew: ונמסרו לעמי הארץ - שלא מסרו לב"ד למנות שומרין לדבר, והאמינה תורה את כל אדם עליהן. והן הן גופי תורה — שחברים אוכלין פתן, וסומכין שניטל ממנו חלה ותרומה ומעשרות. והקדש נמי מסור לכל אדם להקדיש, וחל הקדש ע"פ כל אדם. והן גופי תורה — שהיינו צריכים לחוש במטלטלין שמא הקדישו וחזר בו. ואע"ג דתקון רבנן דמאי, מ"מ תורה האמינתו. ורבותי מפרשים: הלכות הקדש — כגון יין לנסכים, כדמפרש בחומר בקדש (חגיגה דף כז:), שעמי הארץ נאמנים עליו. וקשיא לי: אי מדרבנן קאמר, דחשיב מאי דהימנוהו רבנן, לא הוה ליה למיתני תרומות ומעשרות, דרבנן לא הימנוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:1:1.english: And they were given over to ignoramuses - That [the Torah] did not hand [them] over to the court to appoint overseers for the matter, and the Torah trusted every person regarding them. And these are the very essence of the Torah — for chaverim eat their bread and rely that challah, terumah, and tithes have been separated from it. And hekdesh [consecrated property], too, is handed over to every person to consecrate, and consecration takes effect based on the word of any person; and they are fundamental matters of the Torah, as we would [otherwise] have had to be concerned regarding movable property, lest he consecrated it and retracted. And even though the Rabbis instituted demai, nevertheless the Torah trusted him. And my teachers explain "the laws of hekdesh" [as referring to cases] such as wine for libations, as is explained in [the chapter entitled] Chomer BaKodesh (Chagigah 27b), that amei ha'aretz are believed regarding it. But it is difficult to me: If it is speaking of Rabbinic law, counting what the Rabbis trusted him with, it should not have taught terumot and tithes, for the Rabbis did not trust him [concerning them]!

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:1.english: If you have not the wherewithal to pay - Burnt-offerings and consecrated items that you vow.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:3.hebrew: אל תתן את פיך - בנדר. ״לחטיא את בשרך״ — לחייב את בניך:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:3.english: Suffer not your mouth - Through a vow. "To bring your flesh into guilt" — to make your children liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:4.english: Before the messenger - The treasurer of consecrated property.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:5.hebrew: כי שגגה - בשוגג קפצתי לנדור, ולא אשלם:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:5.english: That it was an error - [Saying,] “In error I rushed to vow, and I will not pay.”

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:2:6.english: At your voice - On account of the sound of your vows.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:1.hebrew: לשוא הכיתי - בתמיה: וכי בחנם הכיתים? אינו אלא בשביל המוסר — דהיינו תורה — לא לקחו. לא למדו — לשון לקח:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:1.english: In vain have I smitten - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question: Did I smite them for nothing? It is only because they did not receive instruction — that is, Torah. [That is,] they did not learn, an expression of instruction [lekach].

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:2.hebrew: על עסקי שוא - ששקרו בנדריהם, דדמי לשבועה:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:2.english: On matters of vanity - That they were false in their vows, which is similar to an oath.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:3.hebrew: והא בעון נדרים אמר - בברייתא קמייתא. ומשני: ההיא קמייתא בתר הך איתמר, דמעיקרא אמר בעון ביטול תורה, ובתר דשמע מר' אלעזר — דשמע מר' שמעון אבוה, דהוה רביה דרבי — בעון נדרים, אמר איהו נמי הכי:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:3:3.english: And didn't he say, "Due to the sin of vows" - In the first *baraita*. And [the Gemara] answers: That first [*baraita*] was stated after this [one], for initially he said, "[Due to] the sin of dereliction in the study of Torah," and after he heard from Rabbi Elazar — who heard from Rabbi Shimon his father, who was Rabbi's teacher — "[Due to] the sin of vows," he too said thus.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:4:1.hebrew: מקרא נדרש - "למען ירבו ימיכם וימי בניכם" נדרש לפניו: קאי אקרא דלקמיה דמשתעי במזוזה, ולא לפני פניו — "ולמדתם אותם את בניכם":
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:4:1.english: A verse is interpreted - "[That] your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children" is interpreted [in connection with the verse] before it: it refers to the verse preceding it, which deals with *mezuza*; and not [with the verse] before the one preceding it — "And you shall teach them to your children."

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:4:2.english: And [to the verse] before the one preceding it - He means [that children die] for the sin of dereliction in Torah study as well.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:5:1.hebrew: גם בכנפיך - בשביל כנפיך שבטלת מצותם, נמצאו עליך חובת דם נפשות אביונים נקיים — בנים קטנים שלא חטאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:5:1.english: Also in your corners - Because of your corners, whose commandment you neglected, there is found upon you the guilt for the blood of the souls of the innocent poor — young children who have not sinned.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:5:2.hebrew: כמחתרת - שאין לה פצימין. הכי אמר קרא: לא במחתרת פתחיהן, מצאתים שלמים במצותי. ״כי על כל אלה״ — הכיתי, דהאי קרא בתר ״לשוא הכיתי את בניכם״ כתיב:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:5:2.english: Like a breach - Which has no doorposts. This is what the verse is saying: Not like a breach were their entrances; I found them complete in My commandments. “For all these” — I struck [them], for this verse is written after “In vain have I smitten your children.”

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:6:1.hebrew: בכנף איש יהודי - בשכר הכנף, יחזיקו בכנף עשרה אנשים מכל לשון — הרי שבע מאות לשבעים לשון, וארבע כנפות יש לו — הרי אלפים ושמנה מאות:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:6:1.english: Of the corner of a Jewish man - As a reward for the mitzvah on the corner, ten men from every language will take hold of the corner — behold, seven hundred for the seventy languages; and he has four corners — behold, two thousand eight hundred.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:1.hebrew: שנאת חנם - שלא ראה בו דבר עבירה שיהא מותר לשנאותו, ושונאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:1.english: Gratuitous hatred - Where he did not see in him a matter of transgression such that it would be permitted to hate him, and [yet] he hates him:

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:2.english: Great discord - [This is] measure for measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:3.hebrew: ובניו קטנים מתים - אהבתו ניטלת ממנו, היינו נמי במדה:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:3.english: And his young children die - His love is taken from him; this too is [measure] for measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:4.hebrew: במכונס - באוצרות יין ושמן, ומתוך כך באה מארה בשערים — שמוכרים ביוקר:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:4.english: In that which is gathered - In storehouses of wine and oil. And as a result of this, a curse comes upon the market prices — that they sell at high prices.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:5.hebrew: והפקדתי - כמו ״לא נפקד ממנו איש״ (במדבר ל״א:מ״ט-נ׳) — אמעט את מה שעליכם, שכנסתם כבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:7:5.english: And I will appoint - [This is] like “not a man of us was missing” (Numbers 31:49–50) — I will diminish that which is in your possession, which you have already gathered.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:8:1.hebrew: השמים נעצרים - ומתוך שאין גשמים, היוקר הוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:8:1.english: The heavens are prevented - And since there is no rain, high prices occur.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:8:2.english: And profit is lost - [The word] sekhar [means] profit.

Rashi on Shabbat 32b:8:3.hebrew: ציה גם חום - ציה, כמו צווי: דברים שצויתי אתכם בשעת החום — היינו תרומות ומעשרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 32b:8:3.english: Drought and heat - “Tziyyah” is like tzivui [commandment]: things that I commanded you at the time of the heat — that is, terumot and tithes.

Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:3:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה הנשיא היינו רבי ורבי בעון נדרים קאמר - והכא לא משני דאף בעון ביטול תורה קאמר, כדמשני לקמן (שבת דף לג:) גבי אף על לשון הרע. דהתם שייך למימר דאף קאמר, דבברייתא שניה שמביא אחריה קאי נמי אתנא קמא דקאמר על לשון הרע, וקאמר איהו: אף שאוכלים דברים שאינם מתוקנים. אבל הכא, אי אף קאמר — א"כ ברייתא דלעיל, דלא קאי את"ק, הוה ליה למינקט נמי בעון ביטול תורה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:3:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is Rabbi, and Rabbi said [that they die] for the sin of vows - And here, [the Gemara] does not answer that he meant [that it is] also for the sin of dereliction in Torah study, as it answers below (Shabbat 33b) regarding "also for slander." For there, it is fitting to say that he meant "also," since in the second baraita that [the Gemara] cites after it, he is also addressing the first Tanna who said [it is] for slander, and he said: [It is] also because they eat foods that are not [ritually] prepared. But here, if he meant "also" — if so, the baraita above, where he is not addressing a first Tanna, should have also mentioned: "for the sin of dereliction in Torah study."

Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:4:1.hebrew: מקרא נדרש לפניו ולפני פניו - תימה לר"י: דבפ"ק דקדושין (דף לד. ושם), דאמר: "כל מצות עשה..." כו', ופריך: "ונקיש מזוזה לתלמוד תורה" — פי': וליפטרי נשים ממזוזה כי היכי דפטירי מתלמוד תורה; ומשני: "לא ס"ד, דכתיב: 'למען ירבו ימיכם' וגו' — אטו גברי בעו חיי, נשי לא בעו חיי?!" והשתא, הא קאי נמי אתלמוד תורה, כדמשמע הכא, אע"פ שאין הנשים חייבות! וי"ל: דבת"ת הוה מחייבינן נמי מהאי טעמא, אי לא מיעט קרא בהדיא, דכתיב: "ולמדתם אותם את בניכם" — ולא את בנותיכם; אבל במזוזה, דליכא מיעוט אלא היקשא, מהאי טעמא אית לן למימר דאין להקיש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:4:1.english: A verse is interpreted homiletically based on [the verse] preceding it as well as [the verse] before the one preceding it - The Ri finds it astonishing: For in the first chapter of Kiddushin (34a and there), where it says "Every positive commandment..." etc., and [the Gemara] challenges: "Let us juxtapose mezuza to Torah study" — explanation: and let women be exempt from mezuza just as they are exempt from Torah study; and [the Gemara] answers: "It cannot enter your mind, for it is written: 'That your days may be multiplied' and so forth — do men require life, while women do not require life?!" And now, does this [verse] not also apply to Torah study, as is implied here, even though women are not obligated [in it]?! And one can say that regarding Torah study we would also have obligated [women] for this [very] reason, had the verse not explicitly excluded [them], as it is written: "And you shall teach them to your sons" — and not to your daughters; but regarding mezuza, where there is no exclusion, but rather [only] a juxtaposition, for this reason we must say that we do not juxtapose [them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:5:1.hebrew: בעון ציצית כו' - דוקא בימיהם, שהיו מלבושיהם כך בארבע כנפות, היו נענשים מי שלא היה להם ציצית, כדמוכח (מנחות מא) גבי א"ל מלאכא לרב קטינא כו'. אבל השתא, שאין העולם רגילים במלבושים כאלו, אין צריך לקנות. אך טוב לקנות טלית ולברך עליו בכל יום, כדאמר בסוף פרק קמא דסוטה (דף יד.): "וכי לאכול מפריה היה רוצה משה? אלא אמר משה: מצוה שאוכל לקיים — יתקיים על ידי". [ת"י]:
Tosafot on Shabbat 32b:5:1.english: "Due to the sin of ritual fringes, etc." - It was specifically in their days, when their garments were like this, with four corners, that those who did not have tzitzit were punished, as is demonstrated in Menachot (41a) regarding [what] the angel said to Rav Ketina, etc. But now, when people are not accustomed to such garments, one is not required to purchase [one]. Nevertheless, it is good to purchase a tallit and recite a blessing over it each day, as [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Sotah (14a): "Did Moses desire to eat of its fruit? Rather, Moses said: A mitzvah that I am able to fulfill, let it be fulfilled through me!" [Tosafot Yeshanim].
